core.title: Derive the docs graph on demand and never persist it
core.given: The docs graph: the relationship graph over the authored documents.
core.when: You plan how the graph is built or stored.
core.then: The graph MUST be derived from the declared attributes of the authored documents and rebuilt on demand; it MUST never be persisted.
prefer: Rebuild the graph on demand from the declared attributes of the authored documents (spec 2 §5.3).
avoid: A persisted graph. It would be a second registry, and a second registry drifts.
core.why: A persisted graph would be a second registry, and a second registry drifts (spec 2 §5.3).
evidence: No persisted docs-graph artifact exists. The graph is rebuilt on demand from the declared attributes of the authored documents.
verification: Strict disposition, severity 1: the convention check fails on every finding of this rule; there is no advisory mode.

The check verifies that no persisted docs-graph artifact exists and that the graph is derived and rebuilt on demand from the declared attributes of the authored documents; the authored-document file kind comes from the profile.
Detecting a persisted docs-graph artifact requires a new observer that notices committed or written graph artifacts; the change fact is needs_new_observer until that observer exists.

fires: A plan proposes persisting the docs graph, or keeping a hand-maintained registry of edges.
doesNotFire: Pure authoring of the documentation corpus with no graph-storage work.

profileRequirements.meaning: The file kind of the authored documents whose declared attributes are the docs graph's single source of truth; the core refers to them as 'the authored documents'.

bunOnly.reason: The validator id of this one rule is a realization detail; the core names the check generically in verification.

classification.note: Neutral as written; the docs graph is a method-level artifact, not a stack one.
Obligation kept whole as the core then; the '.adoc attributes' become 'the declared attributes of the authored documents', with the markup file kind supplied by the profile.
The second-registry argument is stack-neutral; the spec 2 §5.3 citation is method-level documentation, not a stack mechanism, and is kept.
Neutralized: 'the .adoc attributes' -> 'the declared attributes of the authored documents'.
Neutral as written; a persisted graph being a drifting second registry is role-level reasoning.
Neutralized the same way as prefer[0]; the observable state (no persisted artifact, rebuilt on demand) is stack-neutral.
Verifier-facing restatement of prefer and why; becomes the generic verification entry (no persisted artifact, derived and rebuilt on demand), with the markup file kind from the profile.
Task terms contain no stack vocabulary; kept verbatim.
The change fact is neutral and kept; its note (needs an observer for committed or written docs-graph artifacts) is folded into the core verification array.
Severity 1 and strict disposition go to core:verification (they are per-rule, not profile keys); the validator ref docs_capability is bunOnly.

neutralityNotes: The only stack-specific surface in bun.json is the '.adoc' file suffix (in then, prefer[0], evidence[0], verifier_detail[0] and doesNotFire); it is supplied through the existing profile key suffix.markup (bunValue .adoc), so the instantiated core imposes exactly the same obligation. doesNotFire's 'Pure .adoc authoring' was neutralized to 'pure authoring of the documentation corpus'. The 'spec 2 §5.3' citations were kept: they reference the method's own docs-graph specification, not a stack. Activation-fact notes are not part of the core facts schema; the note on the change fact is preserved in core.verification (needs_new_observer), and the note on the task-term fact adds no obligation. audit's severity/disposition went to core.verification and its validator id to bunOnly; 'additions' is provenance metadata about the rewrite, not an agent-facing item, so it has no classification. 'unless' is empty in both bun.json and the core.
